claim: Amy Coney Barrett's nomination to the Supreme Court would be confirmed in October 2020, by a Senate majority that represents 15 million fewer people than the minority party.

sub_claims.question: Was Amy Coney Barrett confirmed to the U.S. Supreme Court in October 2020?
sub_claims.answer: Yes. Amy Coney Barrett was confirmed by the U.S. Senate on October 26, 2020, after being nominated by President Trump following the death of Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg.

evidence.statement: The United States Senate voted to confirm Amy Coney Barrett as an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court on October 26, 2020, by a vote of 52-48.

sub_claims.question: Did the Senate majority that voted to confirm Barrett represent approximately 15 million fewer people than the minority party?
sub_claims.answer: Yes. Analyses of the 2020 confirmation vote showed that the 52 senators who voted to confirm (all Republicans, plus one Democrat who voted present) represented about 143 million people, while the 48 senators who voted against (all Democrats and two independents) represented about 158 million people. This is a difference of roughly 15 million, confirming the claim.

evidence.statement: Analyses of the 2020 U.S. Senate vote on the confirmation of Amy Coney Barrett showed that the 52 senators who voted 'yea' represented an estimated 143 million people, while the 48 senators who voted 'nay' represented an estimated 158 million people.
